name: Parthian
notes: STUB — no grapheme inventory modelled. Parthian (Arsacid Pahlavi, Pahlawānīg), a Northwestern Middle Iranian language, the language of state of the Parthian/Arsacid Empire (248 BCE-224 CE) and later of Manichaean scripture. Like Middle Persian it is written in a Pahlavi-derived Aramaeographic abjad (Inscriptional Parthian and Book/Manichaean Parthian varieties), where many words are spelled as frozen Aramaic logograms ('huzvarishn') read aloud in Parthian — the same orthographic complexity noted for pal.json (Middle Persian) — compounded by two divergent script traditions (Inscriptional Parthian vs. the clearer Manichaean-script Parthian corpus) whose letter inventories and value assignments are not identical. Because the two traditions do not share one clean letter-to-IPA table the way Hoffmann's transliteration does for Avestan, this spec is an honest stub rather than a guessed inventory. Added so it resolves as an ancestry/contact node for Northwestern Middle Iranian and as a sibling to Middle Persian (pal) and Old Persian (peo) in the Iranian ancestry chain.
